title: Conditionals
description: Learn how if, else, and elif control which code runs

exercises.title: The If Statement
exercises.content: This is an 'if' statement. You can read it like this: 'If a equals b, print yes'. Notice that the print("yes") is indented — that's important! Any lines indented under the 'if' statement are part of that statement.
exercises.code:
a = 5
b = 5
if a == b:
    print("yes")

highlights.note: The 'if' keyword starts a conditional check. The part after 'if' and before the colon is the condition.
This line is indented with 4 spaces — it only runs if the condition is True.

exercises.title: Watch: If (True)
exercises.code:
a = 5
b = 5
if a == b:
    print("yes")

exercises.title: Watch: If (False)
exercises.code:
a = 5
b = 3
if a == b:
    print("yes")
print("done")

exercises.question: Write an if statement that prints "hello" if greeting is True
exercises.starterCode:
greeting = True
# write your if statement below

exercises.title: The Else Statement
exercises.content: Sometimes you want to do one thing when a condition is True, and something different when it's False. That's what 'else' is for! The else block runs only when the if condition is False.

highlights.note: The 'if' block runs when the condition is True.
The 'else' block runs when the condition is False. Notice it lines up with the 'if' — same indentation level.

exercises.title: Watch: If/Else (True branch)
Watch: If/Else (False branch)

exercises.question: What does this code print?
Write code: if lives equals 0, print "Game Over", otherwise print "Keep going!"

exercises.title: Comparison Operators
exercises.content: So far we've used == (equals) and >= (greater than or equal). Here are all the comparison operators you can use in if statements. Each one compares two values and gives you True or False.
exercises.code:
a = 10
b = 5
print(a == b)   # Equal? False
print(a != b)   # Not equal? True
print(a > b)    # Greater? True
print(a < b)    # Less? False
print(a >= b)   # Greater or equal? True
print(a <= b)   # Less or equal? False

highlights.note: == checks if two values are equal. Don't confuse with = which assigns a value!
!= checks if two values are NOT equal.
>, <, >=, <= compare which value is bigger or smaller.

exercises.title: The Elif Statement
exercises.content: What if you have more than two options? Use 'elif' (short for 'else if') to check another condition. Python checks each condition from top to bottom and runs the FIRST one that is True. The rest are skipped.

highlights.note: First check: is grade >= 90? If True, print A and skip everything else.
'elif' means 'else if'. Only checked if the previous conditions were False.
The 'else' at the end catches everything that didn't match above.

exercises.title: Watch: If/Elif/Else
